title: Production system
description: JSON Schema for a production system — the Chomsky quadruple (V, T, P, S) of variables, terminals, productions, and a start symbol (Chomsky 1959). A grammar (e.g., the project's name-grammar) specializes a production system by attaching resolution-conformance rules to its terminals. Each inner production has shape {lhs, rhs} with lhs a variable and rhs a sequence of variables and terminals; unevaluatedProperties on the inner production locks its surface so stray fields are rejected.

variables.description: The set V of nonterminal symbols. Each variable is a name; the set is non-empty and contains no duplicates.

terminals.description: The set T of terminal symbols. Disjoint from the variable set (the disjointness condition is universally quantified and checked by the production-system-axiom transformer, not by JSON Schema).

productions.description: The production set P. Each production rewrites a variable (lhs) to a sequence of variables and terminals (rhs). The production array is non-empty (a grammar with no productions cannot generate any string).

lhs.description: The variable being rewritten. Must be a member of the variables array (the membership constraint is checked by the production-membership transformer).

rhs.description: The replacement sequence. Each element is either a variable name or a terminal; the classification is determined by lookup in the parent variables and terminals arrays.

start.description: The start symbol S. Must be a member of the variables array.
